Delivery authorization for harness auto-delivery comes from the workflow's [delivery] policy, never from caller-side allow_publish (which is not persisted). A session-start sweep (workflowToolServiceWithBus, provider != nil) publishes delivery_pending runs left over from a restart/crash; the settlement repair loop ignores allow_publish.

- Reused the claim/flock machinery: reconcile serializes per-run via beginWorkflowExecution, so it never races a live deliverer

- Caller-side allow_publish was never persisted anywhere, so no post-restart sweep could be authorized before this change

Runs park at delivery_pending only when their workflow declares a delivery policy, so that policy is the only durable grant. # Orchestration guardrails: sub-agents stall without committing

scope: project
verdict: mixed
tags: orchestration, spawn_agent, guardrails, commit-discipline, concurrent-writer
created: 2026-08-13

## Summary
Spawned go-engineer agents stalled twice on multi-feature tasks: s3 looped 30+ min on test fixes without committing; s5 ended its run having staged (git add) but never committed. Both required root takeover to finalize. Hard guardrails fixed it: commit-first-green, hard time-boxes (20-25 min), max 2 fix attempts then stop-and-report.

## What worked
- Commit-first-green guardrail produced fast, clean commits (s6b done in 2 min)
- Steer with interrupt=true successfully broke s3 out of its loop
- Checking git status + staged diff at run end recovered s5's staged work
- Full-tree fresh verification (go test -count=1 ./...) caught everything before reporting done

## What did not work
- s3 ran 30+ min with no commit, no parks, no retries — silent spin
- s5 staged its commit but the task completed without finalizing it
- Docs agent never committed its deliverables (had to be committed by root)
- Event ledger records only start events; completion is invisible there — git log is ground truth

## Why
Large spawned tasks (controller admission, driver CLI) loop silently on failing tests — no parks/retries/blocked events appear, so the event ledger gives no signal. Work is at risk from a concurrent writer that restores older file snapshots; uncommitted files can vanish. Root must verify git status + index state at run end, not just task statuses: staged-but-uncommitted work is common (s5 staged 1356 lines then ended). Always include explicit commit instructions in every task prompt (docs agents won't commit otherwise) and re-verify the final tree yourself.

# Provider retry gaps: in-band 200 error envelopes classified permanent

scope: project
verdict: mixed
tags: provider, retry, transient, llmgateway, streaming, error-classification
created: 2026-08-16

## Summary
mivia retries HTTP 5xx/429/502/503/504 at transport (5 attempts) and gates step retries on provider.IsTransient, which classifies envelope errors by text phrase ("http 500"), not type/code. A server_error in-band on a 200 SSE chunk is not transient, so the turn dies permanently. LLM Gateway "Inference request timed out" (500, server_error, internal_error) is retryable by nature.

## What worked
- Transport layer (internal/provider/retry.go) already retries plain HTTP 500 five times with 200ms-5s backoff
- z.ai shows the right pattern: per-provider ErrorParser + NonRetryable + markPermanent, one classifier shared between transport and callers
- Coordinator/workflow step retries (10s/30s/60s backoff) exist and only need IsTransient(err)==true to fire

## What did not work
- Envelope classification relies on the transientMessages phrase table ("http 500"), so a server_error in-band on a 200 SSE chunk is classified permanent and step retry refuses
- Stream error paths return the error without the retryWithoutStreaming fallback (that only fires when err==nil and nothing received)
- llmgateway uses the shared openaiErrorParser; type=server_error, code=internal_error are dropped
- Retry-After honored only for 429/503; transport window (~3s) is far shorter than a gateway upstream inference timeout (LLM Gateway: 10min non-stream, 20min stream)

## Why
Any step that streams (FinalWriter attached = default interactive path) can receive the gateway's error as a 200 SSE chunk after the 200 status is already sent. The typed marker must carry transience, not the message text. Centralized fix: structured classification (status + type + code) in the shared parser, consumed by transport, parser, and IsTransient.

- internal/provider/retry.go
- internal/provider/transient.go

scope: project

## Summary
Context management for panel reviews: reordered the 6 panel member templates so instructions lead and the review target (findings + implementation) sits at the end (recency beats lost-in-the-middle), and tightened bug-fix.toml binding caps (scope 4K, findings 16K). Members already use the industry-standard patterns (structured outputs, parallel specialization, selective fetch).

- Template text controls binding render order (template.Render expands {{ }} in file order): "lost in the middle" (arXiv 2307.03172) is fixable by reordering sections — instructions first, review target (findings/implementation) last, plan in the middle

- Contract tests assert member config paths only, not template content — template reordering is test-safe

## What did not work
- Compaction/summarization is lossy and compounds (Claude Code ~20K token summary reservation; Codex compaction fragile) — use as last resort, not primary strategy
- Per-member binding scoping (security gets no plan) is an engine change (step-level bindings are shared) — deferred
- "Avrix" is NOT a code review product; only an AI-infrastructure firm (avrix.com) — user likely meant Aider/CodeRabbit-class tools

## Why
Industry research (Claude Code/Aider/Cline/Codex/Cursor + G-Research, arXiv 2307.03172) shows focused prompts beat long ones and the most important content must be at the start/end. Our pipeline already had structured context, envelopes, and per-member specialization; the two real wins were ordering and worst-case caps. ## Summary
CORRECTION: on_diff_size_failure is a [delivery] repair-STEP name, never a dead-fail enum. An over-limit diff is a repairable DiffSizeError routed to the repair step (fallback on_failure): the agent shrinks/splits the chunk, delivery retries, bounded by max_repairs. The run is never failed for size alone.

## What worked
- Verified ground truth in code before answering: types.go Delivery.OnDiffSizeFailure (step name), delivery/repair.go RepairTarget (DiffSizeError -> OnDiffSizeFailure -> OnFailure), delivery/stacking.go checkChunkDiffSize (repairable DiffSizeError), controller linear_diff_gate.go (post-implement reroute to the repair step).
- Corrected docs/architecture/workflows.md + docs/product/workflows-guide.md (removed the bogus [stacking] key; added the [delivery] table row).
- Strengthened repair.md + bugfix-repair.md: a DIFF-SIZE rejection is a SPLIT request - shrink the delivered diff, record deferred scope in summary for a follow-up chunk, never silently drop scope.

## What did not work
- My earlier summary/memory claimed an enum on_diff_size_failure = shrink_retry|reroute_fail_fast with a dead-fail mode. That enum DOES NOT EXIST in the code: on_diff_size_failure is a [delivery] knob naming a repair STEP (same pattern as on_failure/on_pr_metadata_failure). The docs I wrote for it were wrong and have been corrected.
- A single inline run can only SHRINK its own delivered diff; turning deferred scope into additional PRs is the stacking driver's (mivia stack plan/drive) job - be explicit about that boundary rather than implying a single run re-chunks.

## Why
The user caught a real misinformation bug: my docs/summary claimed the system can dead-fail a run for an oversized PR, which is the opposite of what the code does and of what they asked for. Recording the verified semantics prevents repeating the error and documents the honest boundary (single-run shrink vs driver-driven multi-PR breakdown).

## Summary
Built-in ollama provider (cloud + local daemon) landed on master in 10 local commits. Keyless local mode is gated by provider=="ollama" AND literal loopback base_url (IsOllamaLoopback), and the dial is pinned to construction-time-resolved loopback IPs to defeat DNS rebinding. - Resolve-once + pin-every-dial (newLoopbackDialContext) defeats DNS rebinding; redirects and HTTPS go through the same pinned dial (DialTLSContext stays nil)
- Non-vacuous test discipline: F1-F10 coverage tests verified by branch-removal reasoning; vacuous tests caught and fixed (error-text discriminators)

- F1 comment initially mispredicted net.JoinHostPort behavior ("127.0.0.1::" vs "127.0.0.1:" -> connection refused, not missing-port)

The security-critical design: mode inference from base_url must be literal-only (no DNS in the predicate), keyless construction must resolve every localhost address to loopback at construction and pin all dials (redirects, HTTPS, retries) to those IPs, and every relaxed gate must be conjunctive (provider name AND loopback) so non-ollama providers never lose their key/HTTPS requirements. # Windows go subprocess needs LOCALAPPDATA passthrough in filtered env

scope: project
verdict: good
tags: windows, packages.Load, GOCACHE, environment-filtering, codeintel, wine
created: 2026-08-10

## Summary
On Windows, cmd/go locates its build cache via GOCACHE or %LocalAppData%\go-build. A filtered env for go subprocesses that drops LOCALAPPDATA (and lacks GOCACHE, which go test never exports) makes every `go list`/packages.Load die with "build cache is required, but could not be located", yielding zero packages — misreported as "symbol not found". Unix masks it via $HOME/.cache/go-build.

## What worked
- Reproduced the CI failure under wine with a real GOOS=windows test binary; the Linux ELF "probe" binary had silently run natively, not under wine (checked with `file`).\n- Driver-level probe (exec go list with the filtered env) surfaced the exact error text instead of guessing.\n- EqualFold matching for Windows env keys avoids the case trap (LOCALAPPDATA vs LocalAppData).

## What did not work
- First attempt added "LocalAppData" (title case) to the allowlist — did nothing because the real var is LOCALAPPDATA.\n- Debugging through the analyzer's "symbol not found" error wasted time; the load errors are swallowed by design.

## Why
internal/codeintel/analyzerEnv() filtered os.Environ() to a small allowlist to block network access. The allowlist had "LocalAppData" (title case) while Windows sets LOCALAPPDATA, so the variable was dropped; all codeintel symbol queries then failed on Windows CI while passing on Linux/macOS. Fix: pass LOCALAPPDATA through with case-insensitive (EqualFold) matching. Also: `go test` does NOT export GOCACHE/GOMODCACHE/GOROOT to test binaries (verified empirically), and `go test -c` without GOOS=windows builds a HOST (Linux) binary even with a .exe name — verify with `file` before running under wine.

# mivia tool-result context pipeline: spool/ref machinery and gaps

scope: project
verdict: neutral
tags: context-management, tool-results, contentrefs, compaction, elision, architecture
created: 2026-08-12

## Summary
mivia already degrades oversized tool results to content refs (remainder.Spool + contentref + read_output, principal-scoped grants, ledger-backed in prod). Gaps vs industry practice: elision in contextmgr drops bodies irreversibly (no ref), batch budget and per-call caps default OFF, inline-vs-ref decision spread across 4+ sites with independent thresholds, no summary layer.

## What worked
- contentref is a single canonical minter (ref:kind:digest)
- remainder.Spool enforces principal-scoped grants + INV-AG-10 (ref only after store)
- shapeBatch degrades batch results to refs, never fails; derive from prompt budget works
- read_output pages 32 KiB with status not_found/denied/expired
- dual head+tail capture exists for run_command

## What did not work
- contextmgr elideToolResults replaces old bodies with a notice that names no ref (bytes lost, compaction irreversible)
- shipped defaults: MaxToolResultChars=0, BatchResultBudgetBytes=0 -> long sessions grow context to compaction trigger
- thresholds duplicated: elision floor 2048, BatchDegradeFloorBytes 16KiB, inline_output_bytes 4096, read_output page 32KiB
- no summary layer for large tool results (head-only inline is a poor summary for search/grep)
- always-ref would cost an extra LLM turn per fetch and relies on model fetch discipline

## Why
The "replace all tool outputs with refs" idea is half-implemented. Ground truth: pass1 per-call cap (CapWithSpoolRef, MaxToolResultChars default 0=uncapped), pass2 batch budget (BatchResultBudgetBytes default 0=off, -1 derives quarter of prompt budget), compaction at 80% of max_prompt_tokens with elision of old >2KiB bodies into a non-retrievable notice, retention at 50% target. Subagent outputs use inline_output_bytes (default 4096) then output_ref. Refs add a full LLM turn per fetch (latency), and models that do not fetch cause thrashing; industry (Anthropic) uses summary+stored-full and reversible compaction, not always-ref.

# mivia persistence timing: chat transcript turn-boundary, ledger synchronous

scope: project
verdict: good
tags: persistence, ledger, chat-session, durability, sqlite, crash-recovery
created: 2026-08-13

## Summary
Chat transcripts persist only at turn boundaries (rolling _turn_ snapshot at turn end, TUI 60s tick, SaveLast on exit); a mid-turn kill loses the in-flight turn. The run ledger (SQLite WAL, synchronous=FULL) is synchronous write-through per mutation: subagent run/task events and content refs are durable when they occur. The main chat turn never writes to the ledger.

## What worked
- 3 parallel researcher agents produced consistent, evidence-backed reports with file:line
- Direct re-read of session.go:363/418, turn_finish.go:131-141, fencing.go:118-165 confirmed the turn-boundary model
- Ledger durability pinned by tests: idempotency_key_durability_test.go, spool_restart_test.go, close_run_atomicity_test.go

## What did not work
- Task 1 initially over-claimed the 60s TUI tick protects the in-flight turn; corrected on re-check (s.Messages is not updated mid-turn). Confirmed by my own verification.

## Why
The user suspected chat messages/tool calls are not persisted the moment they occur. Investigation (3 parallel researchers + direct verification) confirmed this for the session transcript: data lives only in agent.Loop.Messages (a copy seeded at session.go:363) during a turn; s.Messages is replaced and persisted only in commitPreparedTurn (turn_finish.go:138 -> fencing.go:144 -> save_manager.go SaveAfterTurn). The 60s TUI periodic save (welcome.go:48) snapshots the previous completed turn, not the in-flight one. The run ledger is fully synchronous (storage.go appendStoreEvent -> sqlite.go BeginTx/Commit, synchronous=FULL; coordinator record_results.go persists refs inline). The two surfaces have opposite persistence timing: the key mental model.

# Landing verified workflow work locally when delivery fails

scope: project
verdict: good
tags: workflow, delivery, merge, pr-title, worktree
created: 2026-08-10

## Summary
When a feature-delivery workflow run fails at PR delivery (e.g., PR title policy) and its repair step stalls, don't restart a fresh run: the verified code sits uncommitted in the run's worktree. Commit it on the wf/workflow-… branch (repo hooks gate it), then git merge --no-ff into master.

## What worked
- git -C .mivia/worktrees/<run-id> add -A && commit with conventional message (e.g. feat(cli): …) — pre-commit hook ran TUI invariant tests and passed
- git merge --no-ff wf/workflow-<run-id> -m "feat(cli): merge …" — clean ort merge, no conflicts
- go build ./... passed on merged tree; master stays ahead-of-origin intentionally (local v0.4.0)

## What did not work
- workflow_cancel makes the run terminal; workflow_run resume refuses canceled runs
- workflow_deliver only works on delivery_pending runs, so a canceled run can never publish
- repair_pr_metadata (agent step) stalled with no attempt started for ~30 min; poll events (wf_attempt_started) before trusting "running" status
- ledger_read rejects raw sha256:… refs (malformed); use workflow_inspect for step errors

## Why
feature-delivery runs settle at delivery_pending and only publish when the host calls workflow_deliver(allow_publish=true) — publication is never implicit. Delivery fails on metadata (pr_title must match .mivia/policy/pr-title.toml: feat|fix|docs|chore|refactor|test(scope)?!: …). If the auto-repair step (repair_pr_metadata) never starts an attempt, the run is stuck; canceling makes it terminal (resume requires non-terminal), so the branch holds no commit — files are uncommitted in the worktree. Landing locally preserves all gate-verified work (test_validate/verify/code_validate/preflight gates all passed) with zero re-derivation cost.

# Stacking workflows: synthesize run graph BEFORE the runtime build (empty routing digest bug)

scope: project
verdict: good
tags: workflows, stacking, routing-digest, admission, bugfix
created: 2026-08-13

## Summary
Stacking runs failed at their first synthesized step with "agent task routing snapshot mismatch": the controller synthesized the graph AFTER the runtime build and, lacking a registry, injected runtimes with an EMPTY digest. Fix: synthesize before building step runtimes wherever the registry exists (cli, localengine); controller now refuses admission for missing/digest-less synthesized steps.

## What worked
- Made compiler.SynthesizeStacking idempotent (both synthesized steps + repair loop present => already synthesized).
- Synthesized in cli buildWorkflowController and localengine (fresh + resume) before the runtime build, so decompose/chunk_plan_validate get full registry-resolved runtimes (digest, template, schema) and are pinned into the run snapshot for resume.
- Replaced controller-side runtime fabrication with requireSynthesizedStepRuntimes: admission refuses a synthesized step with a missing or digest-less runtime.
- Regression tests: controller admission guard, CLI runtime pinning, resume round-trip, e2e buildWorkflowController.

## What did not work
- Old design injected synthesized runtimes into the controller without a digest; the agent-handler guard caught it at execution ("routing snapshot mismatch") but the run was already admitted and died mid-flight.
- Controller tests with scripted runners that never validate digests could not see the bug; only a path through the real registry-resolving build would have caught it.
- Edge case: a workflow declaring ALL THREE engine-reserved identifiers (decompose + chunk_plan_validate + decompose_repair) is treated as already-synthesized (documented).

## Why
The controller has no agent registry, so it can never resolve a routing digest — synthesizing there is architecturally impossible to do correctly. Any future entry point that builds StepRuntime maps must synthesize the stacking graph first (compiler.SynthesizeStacking is idempotent via the triple reserved-id check). Test coverage must include a path where registry-resolved digests reach a digest-validating handler; scripted runners that never validate digests cannot see this bug class.

# Mivia pre-commit strict structure gate and context principal pitfalls

scope: project
verdict: mixed
tags: mivia-agent, pre-commit, go-structure, contextstate, principal, testing
created: 2026-08-15

## Summary
Pre-commit check_go_structure runs strict: any function over 80 lines fails the commit. contextstate.NewPrincipal mints a fresh random capability per call, so rebuilds of a "same" principal fail store.Load with principal mismatch; take the principal from session.ContextPreparation() (input.Principal) instead.

## What worked
- Swapped a 33-line manual ContextManager wiring in a test for the shared setupSessionContext helper (semantically identical: enableSessionContext wires principal/structural-prep/committer/Enabled).- Verified tests with the focused go test -run filter before committing so the pre-commit suite stayed green.

## What did not work
- First commit attempt failed: a test function was 81 lines (soft max 80, strict mode).- Reconstructing the principal with NewPrincipal(contextWorkspaceID(root), sessionID, \"local-user\") failed store.Load with \"principal mismatch\" because NewPrincipal mints a random capability each call.

## Why
Two recurring gotchas in mivia-agent: (1) commit gate promotes the 80-line soft max to a hard failure, so new tests must stay <= 80 lines per function (factor setup into helpers like setupSessionContext); (2) Principal is capability-bearing and non-reproducible, so durable-store assertions in tests must reuse the session's own principal via _, input, ok := session.ContextPreparation(); store.Load(ctx, input.Principal, sessionID), not reconstruct NewPrincipal(contextWorkspaceID(root), ...).

## References
- internal/cli/tui_force_send_integration_test.go
- internal/contextstate/contracts.go

## Summary
Set ollama (127.0.0.1:11434) model to 131072-token context on a 16GB RTX 5080 by creating a derived model qwen3.6:27b-q4_K_M-128k via /api/create with {"model","from","parameters":{"num_ctx":131072}}. Verified via /api/ps context_length=131072, ~12.5 GiB VRAM, system RAM fine.

## What worked
- /api/create with {"model": name, "from": base, "parameters": {"num_ctx": 131072}} worked instantly (stream:false).
- /api/ps confirms loaded context_length: 131072 and size_vram 12.5 GiB.
- Force-load via a tiny /api/chat call, then check /api/ps; load took ~14s and inference works.

## What did not work
- Legacy {"modelfile": "FROM ...\\nPARAMETER num_ctx ..."} form is rejected by the new create API.
- nvidia-smi is not on the tool allowlist; use /api/ps (size_vram) instead.

## Why
This ollama version's /api/create rejects the legacy Modelfile string ("neither 'from' or 'files' was specified") and requires top-level from + parameters. Also: qwen3.5/qwen35 is a hybrid SSM+attention arch (full attention every 4th block), so its KV cache at 131072 is ~1/4 of a pure-attention 27B and fits in the remaining VRAM of a 16 GB card alongside the 12.5 GiB weights — contrary to the naive 8 GiB KV estimate.

# Stacking plan-run publication is opt-in via delivery.deliver_plan_run (default false)

scope: project
verdict: good
tags: workflows, stacking, delivery, plan-run, config
created: 2026-08-13

## Summary
A stacking plan run is the stack root, not a deliverable: after its chunk stack drives, the plan run settles succeeded and is NOT published unless the workflow sets delivery.deliver_plan_run=true. Plan and artifacts stay in the ledger either way.

## What worked
- Default-false bool keeps existing stacking workflows' behavior unchanged\n- CLI and session surfaces both route through one compiledDeliverPlanRun check\n- Tests: workflow_stack_drive_order_test.go covers CLI + session + drive contract for both settings

## What did not work
- parseRunLine had to change from first-match to last-match; any code assuming the first run_id line is the final state would misread the skip path

## Why
Drive-before-delivery ordering is load-bearing: a multi-chunk plan run settles at delivery_pending (delivery-policy active success terminal), so the chunk stack must drive BEFORE the delivery branch or the plan PR publishes and the stack never drives. The deliver_plan_run option (types.go Delivery struct, toml key) resolves via compiledDeliverPlanRun for the CLI path and is passed into sessionAutoDeliveryRepairLoop for the session path. The skip path CASes the run to succeeded via settlePlanRunSkippedDelivery and prints a second run_id/status line - parseRunLine now takes the LAST such line. Session UI gets run_finished via publishSkippedPlanRunFinished keyed on the seeded stack task ledger (ReadBackPlan), since no delivery record exists.

## References
- internal/workflows/definition/types.go
- internal/cli/workflow_run.go
- internal/cli/session_delivery_repair.go
- internal/cli/workflow_stack_drive_order_test.go

scope: project
verdict: mixed
tags: stacking, workflow, driver, architecture

## Summary
Stacking drive is integrated into `mivia workflow run` itself: after a plan-mode run settles with a multi-chunk plan, the same invocation drives chunk-by-chunk runs (each its own branch/commit/draft PR), waits for merges, then the integration run. No separate drive command.

## What worked
- Hook after Controller.Run settles in executeWorkflowRun: if stacking enabled + decompose output multi, drive to completion\n- driveStackToCompletion loops driveStack passes + waitForChunkMerges polling reconcile/git-merge, then waitIntegrationRunSettled\n- allowPublish threads through driveChunk so chunks publish automatically

## What did not work
- Routing chunk_plan_validate -> implement (one step for all chunks) was wrong: user wants per-task commits/PRs\n- A separate `mivia stack drive` command is rejected: the run must own the stack\n- Backgrounded CLI processes can be killed by canceled tool calls; relaunch with setsid + nohup

## Why
The user rejected both (a) a manual drive command and (b) collapsing multi-chunk plans into one implement step. The requirement: one submission = whole stack, one commit/PR per task, stacked in order, resumable from durable state.
